findings.title: Full tenant takeover via forged CBA certificate

evidence.explanation: A CA in the trust store can sign a certificate whose PrincipalName is a Global Administrator. Low-affinity binding maps that name to the account, and single-factor mode accepts the certificate with no MFA. Reachable Global Administrators: ga@lab.onmicrosoft.com.

authorities.issuer: CN=EntraGoat Rogue CA, O=Contoso Lab, C=US
authorities.reason: Unscoped non-public issuer. This is the higher-risk case: a CA you may not operate can mint tenant logon certificates.

remediation.summary: CESC-1, CESC-2, and CESC-3 together let a trusted CA mint a PrincipalName certificate that signs in as ga@lab.onmicrosoft.com with no password and no MFA. Close all three: high-affinity binding first, multi-factor mode, and remove or scope the CA.
remediation.managedCaNote: After the binding and mode are fixed, replace the rogue CA with a scoped EZCA CA. The forge step works against a CA whose key you hold. It fails against EZCA because that key is HSM-held and is never exported.

evidence.explanation: priority 0 maps PrincipalName to userPrincipalName; priority 1 maps RFC822Name to onPremisesUserPrincipalName. The best high-affinity binding is priority 2, which loses to the low-affinity binding at priority 0. Lower priority numbers are evaluated first. A reusable name on a trusted certificate selects the user.

remediation.summary: Put a high-affinity binding first. Map SubjectKeyIdentifier and SHA1PublicKey to certificateUserIds at priorities 0 and 1, populate certificateUserIds on privileged users, and remove PrincipalName or RFC822Name bindings to userPrincipalName for those accounts.

evidence.explanation: The default CBA mode is x509CertificateSingleFactor. These issuers have no issuerSubject rule forcing x509CertificateMultiFactor: CN=EntraGoat Rogue CA, O=Contoso Lab, C=US.
issuersMissingMfaRule: CN=EntraGoat Rogue CA, O=Contoso Lab, C=US

remediation.summary: Set x509CertificateAuthenticationDefaultMode to x509CertificateMultiFactor, or add an issuerSubject rule that requires multi-factor for every trusted issuer. A certificate alone must not complete sign-in.

evidence.explanation: 1 trusted CA(s) have no certificateAuthorityScopes entry that limits them to a specific group. 1 of them are non-public.

authorities.issuer: CN=EntraGoat Rogue CA, O=Contoso Lab, C=US
authorities.reason: Unscoped non-public issuer. This is the higher-risk case: a CA you may not operate can mint tenant logon certificates.

remediation.summary: Remove every CA you do not operate (CN=EntraGoat Rogue CA, O=Contoso Lab, C=US). The classic trust store does not support update: delete and recreate organization/{id}/certificateBasedAuthConfiguration (fixed id 29728ade-6ae4-4ee9-9103-412912537da5), and do not send the read-only issuer or issuerSki fields. Scope every CA you keep with certificateAuthorityScopes to a specific group, not all_users. Replace 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 with that group's object id.
remediation.managedCaNote: A scoped managed CA such as Keytos EZCA closes CESC-3 by design: the signing key stays in an HSM and is never exported, and certificateAuthorityScopes limit which group that CA can authenticate.

findings.title: CRL validation disabled or certificate authorities exempted

evidence.explanation: crlValidationConfiguration.state is disabled. Revoked certificates keep working.

remediation.summary: Set crlValidationConfiguration.state to enabled, clear exemptedCertificateAuthoritiesSubjectKeyIdentifiers, and publish a CDP the tenant can reach. Revoked certificates must fail sign-in.

findings.title: Intune certificate profile with a spoofable subject or SAN

evidence.explanation: SCEP or PKCS enrollment builds an identity from device attributes an attacker can influence, without the on-premises security identifier. This is the cloud shape of AD CS ESC1.

profiles.reason: Subject or SAN is built from a spoofable device attribute and strong SID mapping is off.

remediation.summary: Stop building the subject or SAN from {{DeviceName}}, {{FullyQualifiedDomainName}}, {{SerialNumber}}, or {{IMEI}}. Put the on-premises security identifier in the subject or SAN and turn on strong name mapping.

findings.title: Intune certificate in a shared store or with over-broad usage

evidence.explanation: A certificate any app can use, or one with anyPurpose, serverAuth plus clientAuth, or CA key usage, widens what a stolen device key can do.

profiles.reason: The certificate is in the VPN and apps store and the usage or EKU is over-broad.

remediation.summary: Move the certificate out of the VPN and apps store. Keep key usage at digitalSignature and a single clientAuth EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2). Drop anyPurpose and serverAuth.
